content.value_statement: Phylogenetic biogeography needs strict input formats and careful model setup. This skill prepares validated BioGeoBEARS workflows with documentation and interpretation guidance.
actual_capabilities: Validates BioGeoBEARS geography files and checks species names against tree tips.
Converts CSV or TSV distribution tables into PHYLIP-style geography data.
Creates an organized analysis directory with input, scripts, results, and documentation.
Customizes an RMarkdown BioGeoBEARS workflow with tree, geography, model, and range parameters.
Generates guidance for DEC, DIVALIKE, BAYAREALIKE, and +J model comparison.
Explains output files, AIC weights, parameter estimates, and ancestral range plots.
limitations: Requires user-provided tree and geography files with matching species names.
Does not install R, Python, BioGeoBEARS, or required R packages automatically.
Analysis runtime depends on tree size, number of areas, and selected models.
Scientific interpretation still requires domain review and biological context.

use_cases.title: Prepare island biogeography analyses
use_cases.description: Evolutionary biologists can turn tree and island distribution files into a BioGeoBEARS project.

use_cases.title: Validate distribution data
use_cases.description: Lab analysts can detect formatting problems before running long R analyses.

use_cases.title: Compare ancestral range models
use_cases.description: Graduate researchers can set up DEC, DIVALIKE, BAYAREALIKE, and +J model comparisons.

prompt_templates.title: Start a BioGeoBEARS setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me set up a BioGeoBEARS analysis. Ask for my tree file, geography file, maximum range size, and models.

prompt_templates.title: Validate my geography file
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether my geography file matches my tree tips. Tell me what mismatches or format problems need correction.

prompt_templates.title: Create the analysis workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a BioGeoBEARS project using my rooted tree and distribution table. Use all six models and prepare a report workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Interpret model results
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my BioGeoBEARS report outputs. Explain model support, parameter estimates, likelihood ratio tests, and ancestral range plots for publication.

output_examples.input: A user provides a rooted tree and a CSV distribution table for 30 species across five islands.
output_examples.output: The skill validates names, reformats geography data, creates project folders, prepares the report workflow, and lists run instructions.

output_examples.input: A geography file has spaces in species names and mismatched tree tips.
output_examples.output: The skill reports the mismatches, explains required formatting, and suggests corrected species names before analysis starts.

output_examples.input: A user receives BioGeoBEARS results with similar AIC weights.
output_examples.output: The skill explains model uncertainty, compares support, and recommends reporting multiple models with clear biological context.

best_practices: Validate tree and geography files before rendering the RMarkdown report.
Run all six supported models first, then simplify if runtime is too high.
Document range-size choices, area definitions, and excluded species.
anti_patterns: Do not run analyses with unmatched species names between tree and geography files.
Do not choose maximum range sizes that are biologically impossible.
Do not treat the best AIC model as final without checking parameter estimates.

faq.question: What inputs does this skill need?
faq.answer: It needs a rooted Newick tree and a geography table with species distributions by area.

faq.question: Can it reformat my distribution table?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a script that converts CSV or TSV presence data into BioGeoBEARS geography format.

faq.question: Does it install BioGeoBEARS?
faq.answer: No. It provides installation guidance, but the user environment must install required R packages.

faq.question: Which models can it prepare?
faq.answer: It supports DEC, DEC+J, DIVALIKE, DIVALIKE+J, BAYAREALIKE, and BAYAREALIKE+J workflows.

faq.question: Can it help interpret results?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains AIC weights, parameter estimates, likelihood ratio tests, and ancestral range plots.

faq.question: What affects analysis runtime?
faq.answer: Runtime grows with tree size, number of geographic areas, maximum range size, and selected models.
